```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=5)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
library(broom)
vehicles <- read_csv("data/silverado_1500_clean.csv", show_col_types=FALSE)
set.seed(42)
```

## Executive summary

This analysis examines how **vehicle age** and **mileage** relate to advertised prices of 2010–2019 Chevrolet Silverado 1500 listings in the Southeast. The goal is to explain relationships, compare model complexity, and estimate out-of-sample predictive accuracy. Prices are *asking prices*, not verified transaction prices; associations are not causal.

## Dataset

The provided source CSV is a used-vehicle listings extract. The reproducible portfolio dataset retains Silverado 1500 listings with model years 2010–2019, positive prices, and nonmissing nonnegative mileage. Age is measured relative to **2021**, matching the original coursework's reference year. The dataset includes `r nrow(vehicles)` listings from `r n_distinct(vehicles$state)` states. The analysis below uses this consistent subset for every model; the original homework sometimes used a different model label (`silverado`) and therefore different samples.

```{r preview}
glimpse(vehicles)
summary(vehicles[c("price", "age", "odometer")])
```

## Exploratory data analysis

```{r plots, fig.show='hold'}
ggplot(vehicles, aes(odometer, price)) + geom_point(alpha=.4, color="#2563eb") + geom_smooth(method="lm", se=TRUE, color="#ea580c") + labs(title="Price versus mileage", x="Mileage (miles)", y="Asking price ($)") + theme_minimal()
ggplot(vehicles, aes(age, price)) + geom_jitter(width=.12, alpha=.4, color="#2563eb") + geom_smooth(method="lm", se=TRUE, color="#ea580c") + labs(title="Price versus age", x="Age in 2021 (years)", y="Asking price ($)") + theme_minimal()
```

## Baseline and nonlinear regression

```{r models}
mileage <- lm(price ~ odometer, data=vehicles)
age <- lm(price ~ age, data=vehicles)
additive <- lm(price ~ age + odometer, data=vehicles)
quadratic <- lm(price ~ age + I(age^2), data=vehicles)
second_order <- lm(price ~ age + odometer + I(age^2) + I(odometer^2) + age:odometer, data=vehicles)
model_list <- list("Mileage only"=mileage, "Age only"=age, "Age + mileage"=additive, "Quadratic age"=quadratic, "Complete second order"=second_order)
comparison <- bind_rows(lapply(names(model_list), function(nm) {
 s <- glance(model_list[[nm]])
 data.frame(model=nm, r_squared=s$r.squared, adjusted_r_squared=s$adj.r.squared, AIC=s$AIC)
}))
knitr::kable(comparison, digits=3)
summary(additive)
```

A model with a higher R-squared is not automatically preferable: additional terms can overfit. Use the adjusted R-squared, nested tests for genuinely nested models, and holdout error to assess whether complexity helps.

```{r tests}
anova(mileage, additive)
anova(additive, second_order)
anova(quadratic, second_order)
```

## Residual diagnostics

```{r diagnostics, fig.show='hold'}
par(mfrow=c(1,2))
plot(additive, which=1)
plot(additive, which=2)
par(mfrow=c(1,1))
diagnostics <- data.frame(standardized_residual=rstandard(additive), leverage=hatvalues(additive), cooks_distance=cooks.distance(additive))
head(diagnostics[order(-diagnostics$cooks_distance),], 5)
```

Residual patterns may indicate nonconstant variance, nonnormal errors, or outliers. The table identifies observations worth inspecting rather than automatically deleting them.

## Prediction intervals

```{r intervals}
new_listing <- data.frame(age=5, odometer=60000)
predict(additive, newdata=new_listing, interval="confidence", level=.95)
predict(additive, newdata=new_listing, interval="prediction", level=.95)
```

The confidence interval estimates the **mean** listing price at the specified age and mileage; the prediction interval describes a **single** new listing and is wider.

## Holdout validation

```{r validation}
set.seed(42)
train_idx <- sample(seq_len(nrow(vehicles)), size=floor(.8*nrow(vehicles)))
train <- vehicles[train_idx,]
test <- vehicles[-train_idx,]
formulas <- list("Mileage only"=price~odometer, "Age only"=price~age, "Age + mileage"=price~age+odometer, "Quadratic age"=price~age+I(age^2), "Complete second order"=price~age+odometer+I(age^2)+I(odometer^2)+age:odometer)
metrics <- bind_rows(lapply(names(formulas), function(nm) {
 fit <- lm(formulas[[nm]], data=train)
 predicted <- predict(fit, newdata=test)
 actual <- test$price
 data.frame(model=nm, MAE=mean(abs(actual-predicted)), RMSE=sqrt(mean((actual-predicted)^2)), test_R2=1-sum((actual-predicted)^2)/sum((actual-mean(actual))^2))
}))
knitr::kable(metrics, digits=2)
```

The holdout split is random, not chronological. Results measure performance on a comparable sample of listings, not future market conditions.

## Limitations and next steps

- Listings are not completed sales; listing quality and market conditions are unobserved.
- Age and mileage may be correlated; inspect coefficient stability and collinearity.
- Selection of a single model and year range limits generalizability.
- Improve the study by incorporating trim, condition, location, and listing date; validate on a later time period.

## Reproducibility

Run `source("requirements.R")` once, then `rmarkdown::render("analysis.Rmd")` from the project directory. Data and plots are included in this repository.
